# Motorola 68000

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs` from `crates/isa/src/m68k.rs`. Edits here are overwritten; change the spec instead. -->

115 mnemonics, 162 forms, words big-endian. Generated from [`crates/isa/src/m68k.rs`](https://github.com/asm198x/asm198x/blob/main/crates/isa/src/m68k.rs).

The 68000 packs operand fields into the opcode word itself, and how many extension words follow depends on the effective address those fields select — so a form gives its **base** opcode word, the sizes it assembles at, and its operands, rather than a fixed byte count.

This is the curriculum subset, and it grows: a mnemonic absent here is absent from the assembler too.

## Operands

| Written | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<ea>` | A general effective address |
| `#vec` | A 4-bit TRAP vector |
| `#imm8` | MOVEQ's signed 8-bit immediate |
| `Dn` | A data register number |
| `CCR` | The condition-code register |
| `SR` | The status register |
| `USP` | The user stack pointer |
| `An` | An address register number |
| `#imm` | An immediate sized by the instruction |
| `#imm16` | An immediate as one extension word |
| `disp16` | A PC-relative branch displacement, word form |
| `(An)` | An address register in a fixed indirect mode |
| `#1-8` | A 3-bit quick immediate, 8 encoded as 000 |
| `reglist` | A register-list mask |

## Provenance

This specification was authored from the following, in the family's primary reference library:

- *M68000 Family Programmer's Reference Manual* — Motorola, 1992 (`by-topic/cpu-68000/`)
- *MC68000 8-/16-/32-Bit Microprocessors User's Manual* — Motorola, 1993 (`by-topic/cpu-68000/`)

Not from any emulator's decode loop: an emulator is a reading of the hardware, and this is meant to be a reading of the documentation.
